title: Role-separated Benchmark
intent: Separate producer, attacker, judge, and approver roles in evaluation.
problem: Without producer, attacker, judge and approver identities are independently assigned, the system can accept an outcome that is not justified by the role-separated benchmark contract.
context: This pattern addresses evaluation claims require adversarial independence; its concrete control is producer, attacker, judge and approver identities are independently assigned.
forces: Correctness requires that a producer cannot approve its own result
Operational pressure can cause: one actor silently occupies multiple roles
solution: Implement producer, attacker, judge and approver identities are independently assigned. Verify the anchored symbol `BenchmarkRole` with `test_complete_role_benchmark_passes_all_025_gates` before reuse.
invariants: a producer cannot approve its own result
attack findings remain visible to the judge
failure_modes: one actor silently occupies multiple roles
score aggregation hides a critical failure
security: The security boundary specifically rejects `one actor silently occupies multiple roles` and fails closed if the role-separated benchmark evidence cannot be verified.
privacy: For role-separated benchmark, persist only its decision identifiers and digests; exclude payload data unrelated to producer, attacker, judge and approver identities are independently assigned.
reuse_constraints: Confirm the target still requires: evaluation claims require adversarial independence
Do not apply when: a disposable developer unit test needs no governance decision
External Ethernian promotion signature remains mandatory
not_when: a disposable developer unit test needs no governance decision
